summary: The wake gate now reports what the model is actually hearing, so a gate that has stopped firing can be told apart from a gate hearing nothing.
details: The gate scored every 80ms chunk and reported the number only when it crossed the threshold. Live, that produced 37 armed gates and zero wake fires across four days with no number anywhere to say why — the last fire was 2026-09-17 17:00 and audio kept arriving the whole time (196 frames, zero pump drops, on the attempt that prompted this).

A peak score over a window is now logged per speaker, sampled once per 50 chunks rather than per chunk. The two failures it separates need opposite fixes: a peak near zero means the audio reaching the model is not speech, which is a pipeline fault; a peak just under the threshold means it is speech the model nearly matched, which is a model or microphone fault.

The model itself is not implicated: the shipped 喂Nora.onnx scored 12 of 12 real positives at 0.945-0.992 inside the running production container, so the ONNX runtime, the model file and the threshold are all sound.
limitations: This measures the fault; it does not fix it. Which of the two causes is live is still unknown, and the new log line is what decides it on the next attempt.
